I really enjoyed it when I played the remastered version with "alternative controls". I did play the original way back when, but I got frustrated and annoyed at the "artistic" control scheme and character movement. The remaster included an option for more responsive input, which made the world of difference to me.

As for the actual game design, I really liked the minimalist story telling. Too many games these days are just scripted sequence after scripted sequence that play out like cut-scenes, and all you get in between are actual cut-scenes. SOTC doesn't do that. You have full control in between fighting the Colossi, and you get a cut-scene as a reward for overcoming the challenge, which reveals a bit more of the story.

At first I felt the world was really empty, and it is mostly, but it's also beautiful. But there are also a few small collectibles scattered about to look out for and gather up, as well as shrines to find, so there's content you have be on the look out for. You can speed-run the game from colossi to colossi, but you're missing some very intentional down-time in between that involves finding fruit and lizards and things, and these actually play into the lore quite a bit.

Another thing is that fantasy games often go for that "ancient majesty" feel to their world, but hardly ever pull it off. SOTC managed it quite well, I thought. The ruins are huge and expansive, and do a great job of making the player feel small and alone, whereas too often it's the world that feels small when it's designed around making the player feel powerful.

I also liked that each colossi was essentially a puzzle of moving pieces.

I'm in the minority, I think, when it comes to actually enjoying an empty expanse in a game world. I didn't mind it in BOTW, because part of the fun of adventure is the travel from A to B, as long as the controls are fluid and it just has that "fun" feel to it, and SOTC did have that with the alternative input method. I like exploring for the sake of exploring, I like puzzles, I like minimalist story-telling that explains more via environment and suggestion rather than beating you over the head.

It's not for everyone, and I think it's one of those games that's cool to love because it's so "artsy", so there are a lot of people who go on about the game because it makes top ten lists and they want to feel hip or whatever, but it is a great game if it is your type of game. I can definitely see why people don't like it though, and why people claim to like it when they've never played it.
